κακότητος τοῦ βίου δυσχερείας τοὺς ἀκάκους φυλάσσει· ἀκάκους. δὲ λέγει τοὺς
κακῶς ἔκ τινος ὑπομένοντας, καὶ ἀκακίαν ἀσκοῦν τας ἐν ἀγάπῃ. Ἢ οὕτως.
Ἀνεξέλεγκτος, ἡ πρόσχημα μὲν εὐσεβείας ἔχουσα, ἀγύμναστος δὲ οὖσα καὶ ἀνεξέ
ταστος· ὁ γὰρ μὴ ἐλεγχόμενος, καὶ φανερῶν καὶ ἑτέροις τὰ φρονήματα καὶ τοὺς
διαλογισμοὺς αὐτοῦ, πλανᾶται οἰήσει. Τὸ, καλύπτουσιν, ἀντὶ τοῦ, οὐκ ἐῶσιν
ἀνανεῦσαι. Ἢ ἔχθραν τὴν κακίαν λέγει, δι' ἧς ἐχθροὶ γινόμεθα τοῦ Θεοῦ· τὴν δὲ
κατὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ἀνθρώπων ἔχθραν ἐγγινομένην ἡμῖν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ ὑπὸ τοῦ
πονηροῦ, αὐ τὴν μὲν ἀποσείονται οἱ δίκαιοι, τοῖς δὲ χείλεσι τὸν Θεὸν ὑμνοῦσιν, ὅταν
οὕτως αὐτοῖς ὁ πονηρὸς ὑπο βάλλῃ· Εἰ γὰρ ἐχθροὶ ὄντες, φησὶν ὁ Παῦλος, κατ
ηλλάγημεν τῷ Θεῷ διὰ τοῦ θανάτου τοῦ Υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ· εἰ δὲ ἡ ἔχθρα, κακία ἐστὶν, ἡ
φιλία ἀρετὴ καὶ γνῶσις Θεοῦ, δι' ἧς φίλοι γινόμεθα αὐτοῦ καὶ τῶν ἁγίων δυνάμεων·
ἐπὶ δὲ τῆς φιλίας ταύτης, οἱ ὄντες αὐτοῦ φίλοι, καὶ ἀλλήλων
pass_a_gloss: Life's wickedness burdens the innocent; yet it safeguards them. Or: those who suffer harm from some cause and train in innocence through love. Alternatively: unexamined, showing a pretense of godliness but lacking discipline and trial— for whoever avoids scrutiny, openly sharing thoughts and reasoning with others, strays into self-delusion. The covering, meaning they do not permit revival. Or: He names hatred of evil, by which we become God's enemies; and the enmity toward God and humans arising in our hearts from the evil one— the righteous reject it, while with lips they praise God when the evil one thus subdues them. For if we were enemies, Paul says, we were reconciled to God through His Son's death; but if enmity equals wickedness, then friendship is virtue and knowledge of God, by which we befriend Him and the holy powers; and in this friendship, His friends are mutually friends. Lord, before You all my longing, says David— meaning what pleases God and agrees with the just, we must desire, so our prayer may be acceptable before Him; but the ungodly wanders in eternal ruin by desiring and doing what displeases God. If the fear of the Lord adds days, Wisdom starts with reverence for God; these times are wisdom’s portions, shaped by righteousness’ light. Advancing brings more insight and brightness. David begs not to be taken mid-life. Abraham lived his days fully, dying aged and satisfied. God grants heavenly visions as extra days to faithful believers. Sinners’ years appear empty, lacking grace, thus diminished. Human life spans an age, like Paul refusing meat forever to avoid offending a brother—what sustains life he names an age. The just, even when giving, never fall to evil’s lure. The ungodly who transgress lose not only the realm but inhabit flames, not soil. Oppositely, grace overflows; the devout utter thoughts and heart, lips praising God. The wicked’s foul speech turns from God to evil. Note what flows from each source. Fixated on coming good, the just gains all hoped for at life’s end. Or He guides us toward rising again. Existing things endure in this case, not destroyed; but in that case, even existing things are extinguished, since boasting occurs only in the present age—of whom it is written: "Their glory is in their shame." The statement does not mean the righteous is the basis of justice, claiming "the wicked is handed over instead of him," but rather, because the trap originates from the wicked against the righteous, the wicked falls into it while the righteous remains. God delivers the righteous; the wicked, left behind, falls, as in "the sinner is seized by his own hand's work." Alternatively, if the righteous is regarded by some as a sinful person, the wicked arrives, harms the righteous, escapes sins and future punishments, yet assumes the punishments for himself. He is handed over by his own wickedness, having surrendered himself to an disapproved mind. Either this is judgment about actions to take, or not; or it is to manage their own existence, since it is a vast, helpless flood—such people, blown by every wind, are wrecked in life or faith, falling like tree leaves from God, lacking divine wisdom. But if salvation resides in counsel, not simply counsel, but abundant counsel, then—
pass_b_english:
The wickedness of life oppresses the innocent; it protects the innocent. Yet He speaks of those who endure evil from some source, and who practice innocence in love. Or thus: Unexamined, possessing the pretense of piety but being untested and untried— for the one who is not examined, and who openly reveals his thoughts and reasonings to others, wanders in self-conceit. The covering, instead of not allowing to breathe. Or He speaks of enmity toward wickedness, by which we become enemies of God; and the enmity against God and mankind that arises in us by the evil one in the heart— the righteous indeed shake it off, while with their lips they praise God, whenever the evil one thus subdues them. For if we are enemies, says Paul, we were reconciled to God through the death of His Son; but if the enmity is wickedness, then friendship is virtue and knowledge of God, by which we become friends of Him and of the holy powers; and upon this friendship, those who are His friends are also friends to one another. Lord, before You all my desire is, says David; that is, whatever is pleasing to God and harmonious with the just, one ought to desire, so that our prayer may become acceptable before God; but the ungodly is carried away in eternal destruction by desiring and doing what is not friendly to God. If the fear of the Lord adds days,

The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord; these days are parts of wisdom, made by the sun of righteousness. For one who presses forward adds knowledge and illuminations. Moreover, for such days David prays, saying: Do not bring me to the midst of my days. And these days, Abraham having fulfilled them, died old and full of days. And the Lord adds the divine visions as days to those who are in faith and fearing Him. But the years of the wicked, seen as foolish and devoid of divine grace, have been made little. He speaks of the lifetime of a man as an age, as Paul says: I will not eat meat for the age, lest I scandalize my brother. For that which is added to the constitution of his life, he has called an age. For the righteous does not sin in giving, being troubled by the evil one. But the wicked who sin will not only be cast out of the kingdom, but will dwell in fire and not on the earth. Instead, grace is an overflowing abundance; and the mouth of the pious now speaks the mind and the heart, as if singing hymns to God through the lips. But the mouth speaking evil of the wicked is turned away from God to become that of the evil one. See therefore what comes from that, and what from this. For having the goal toward the future, one certainly attains what was expected, having finished as the righteous. Or He leads us forward to the resurrection.

And concerning this, the existing things remain, and are not destroyed; but concerning that, even the existing things are extinguished. For in the present age alone they boast—of whom it has been said: "Their glory is in their shame." Not as if the righteous one were the subject of justice, saying, "Instead of him, the wicked is delivered up," but because the snare comes from the wicked against the righteous, the wicked falls into it while this one remains. The righteous is snatched away by God, but the wicked, having been abandoned, falls—according to the saying, "The sinner is caught in the works of his own hands." Or because the righteous is thought by some to be a man of sins, the wicked comes and does evil to the righteous; from the sins and the punishments that were to come, he has delivered himself, but for himself he has taken up the punishments. He is delivered over by himself through his own wickedness, as one who has given himself over to an unapproved mind. Either this is discernment concerning things to be done, or not; or so that they may manage their own lives—for it is a great and hopeless wave. For such people, driven about by every wind, suffer shipwreck concerning life or faith; and they fall like leaves from a tree, those who do not possess the wisdom of God.
